Exploratory Data Analysis

Statistical Analysis and Temporal Patterns

Overview

This page presents exploratory data analysis of our Reddit dataset, addressing 3 EDA business questions through statistical analysis, temporal patterns, and visualizations.

Subreddit Popularity

Business Question 1

Question: How popular is a particular subreddit in terms of unique users?

Analysis Approach

  • Group subreddits by city
  • Extract week from created_utc timestamp
  • Calculate unique commenters per week (removing repeat users)
  • Average unique commenters over the year
  • Generate visualizations comparing subreddit popularity

Findings

Key Insight

This bar graph compares the number of unique posters averaged by population size of each city. LA has the most unique users and new york has the fewest throughout the weeks of our data. Interestingly, the cities with the highest population don’t necessarily have the most unique users.

Key Insight

The heatmap shows the normalized number of unique users every week throughout the year in the range of our data. It shows that some subreddits are more event-driven (where people are responding to local news/events with spikes in activity), while other ones have continuously steady, low baseline activity regardless of what’s happening in their cities. An example of the event-driven one is Los Angeles, with several peaks throughout the year and generally high activity from unique users. New York, on the other hand, seems to have a general baseline of unique users without many spikes. The major peak in Houston in late July 2024 matches up with Hurricane Beryl and might be an indication of residents and people from other cities/states trying to communicate with people in Houston. The spikes in late April 2024 might correspond with protests related to Palestine, especially on college campuses whose subreddits were included in this analysis.

Key Insight

The largest subreddits seem to have the most variation in daily users, with New York and LA having the biggest ranges. Houston has the biggest outlier, which matches the finding of the heatmap.

Posting Time

Business Question 2

Question: What time of day do people post the most?

Analysis Approach

  • Take the submissions data and group by the subreddit for each individual city
  • Use the created_utc variable to extract the hour of the day that the post was made and group by the hour
  • Convert the UTC time stamps to the correct time zones based on the location of city that the subreddit corresponds to
  • Count the number of unique submissions made during each hour
  • Create time series plot that depicts the number of posts per hour of the day for each of the individual city subreddits

Findings

In Figure 4, we see the aggregated number of postings per hour. Each of the lines indicate a distinct city and are normalized to the population size of the city and localized for the timezone.

Immediately, we can compare the most popular city for Reddit, which is New York as it has the most posts per hour for every hour of the day. This is followed by Philadelphia, which has the second most number of posts per hour for all hours. Chicago, Los Angeles, and Houston all trade between 3rd, 4th, and 5th number of posts per hour.

The absolute number of postings may differ across cities, however, there seems to be a common trend about the hours of day that are most popular within cities. For all cities, the night hours (between around 11PM to 5AM) are less popular. On the flip side, times between 10AM and 5PM are most popular for almost all cities. The only real outlier to these trends is Houston, which is mostly flat across all hours of the day with only slight peaks around 9AM and 7PM.

Key Insights:

  • Most Reddit users are posting between 10AM and 5PM (local time).
  • Very few users are active during night hours.
  • New York sees the highest number of posters at almost all hours of the day.
  • Houston’s posting numbers are very consistent across all hours.

Highest Scoring Posts

Business Question 3

Question: Which kind of posts get the highest scores?

Analysis Approach

  • Utilize the dataset including all city subreddits
  • Extract the score variable which indicates the number of upvotes minus the number of downvotes on the post
  • Take the top 10% of posts in terms of score
  • Match the post to a pre-specified topic using simple text processing (lowercasing, removing stopwords) and a Regex-based function
  • Count the number of posts in the top 10% belonging to each topic category
  • Create a bar chart that shows the number of high scoring posts across topics categories

Findings

Key Insights:

  • Local sports dominate the top highest score posts across all city subreddits.
  • Pro sports are the second most popular topic in terms of high scoring posts, showing that sports culture is a strong community engagement driver.
  • Besides sports, the third top topic is transportation, indicating that transit issues are a key concern for many city residents.

Temporal Analysis

Posting Patterns Over Time

The biggest traffic for Reddit posting occurs on Wednesday, followed by Thursday and the least popular days are Sunday and Saturday. In terms of time of day, the top posting time is 11AM, while 3AM is the least popular posting time.

Peak Activity Analysis

Hourly Patterns:

  • Peak hours: 11:00 AM, 1:00 PM
  • Lowest activity: 3:00 AM, 4:00 AM

Summary

Answers to EDA Business Questions

  1. Subreddit Popularity: The most popular set of city subreddits normalized by population is Los Angeles, while the least popular is New York.
  2. Posting Time: People seem to post during work hours with the busiest day being Wednesday and there is little variation between cities.
  3. Highest Scoring Posts: Sports-related posts (both local and professional) dominate the highest scoring posts across all cities, followed by transportation topics, indicating strong community engagement around sports culture and transit issues.

Key Takeaways

  • Some city’s subreddits are event driven, with unique users comment when major events happen, while other have a steady baseline of users.
  • Temporal posting patterns show remarkable consistency across all five cities.
  • Across all the cities, sports-related posts tend to receive the highest scores, indicating a strong community interest in local and professional sports.
